definition: Agnostic means believing that the existence of God cannot be proven or disproven.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word agnostic. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know agnostic should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Somewhere in his fifties the barber went agnostic: ask about God while he trims and he claims neither a yes nor a no, because the proof he would need, he says, is not the kind this world supplies.
An open-minded juror can still be won over by either side; agnostic goes further, holding that on this question no ruling can ever be reached.
An undecided voter expects to choose by Election Day; the agnostic position is stronger - it says the deciding evidence can never arrive at all.

Noncommittal means refusing to state a position - a shrug in word form - whatever you may privately believe. Agnostic is not a dodge: it openly stakes a claim, that this question cannot be settled by evidence at all. The noncommittal speaker hides a view; the agnostic announces one.

Neutral means taking no side in a dispute, often to stay fair or above the fray - a referee is neutral by role. Agnostic is not about sides at all: it is a considered claim that the question itself can never be settled by any evidence.

The rash and the fever led the pediatrician to a quick diagnosis.
Agnostic means believing that the existence of God cannot be proven or disproven.
Past midnight, my roommates went back and forth over theology and cold tea - one quoting proofs of design, the other proofs of absence.
Sam, the physics major, refused both chairs.
He was agnostic, he said: for him to say yes, or to say no, something would have to count as a test of God - and nothing ever could.
So he claimed nothing, and poured more tea.
Agnostic is precise here because Sam isn't wavering and isn't disbelieving - he holds the question itself to be beyond evidence.
An atheist claims an answer (no); a believer claims an answer (yes); the agnostic claims the question can't be answered.
That's a position, not a shrug.

Agnostic makes a strong, specific claim: not 'I haven't decided' but 'this question cannot be settled by evidence.' Say undecided for a mind still choosing, and dubious - another word in this unit - when the doubt leans toward disbelief.
Everyday tech talk uses agnostic loosely ('platform-agnostic'), but in careful writing keep it for questions held to be unanswerable.

The dorm's Sunday argument always ended at the same wall.
Marcus believed; Priya did not; and Ana, to everyone's irritation, would not join either camp.
Asked directly, she laid out her position at length: whether God exists is a question, she argued, that no possible evidence could ever settle.
'Show me the experiment,' she would say.
'Any miracle can be doubted, any silence explained.
The scales cannot tip, because nothing in this world can land on them.' Marcus called her agnostic stance lazy.
Ana answered that it was the opposite: she had staked a claim bolder than his, a claim about the limits of proof itself.
Priya kept trying to recruit her, promising one argument that would finally decide it.
The whole point, she said, is that no argument ever could.
